title: Common Causes of Fire Along HDB Corridors and Proportion of HDB Flats with Home Fire Alarm Device Installed
what_it_is: Common Causes of Fire Along HDB Corridors and Proportion of HDB Flats with Home Fire Alarm Device Installed

sections.label: Home Fire Alarm Device rules
sections.summary: New residential units and units undergoing fire safety works must install Home Fire Alarm Devices under the Fire Code, while older units are voluntary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Since June 2018, all new residential units and existing units that are undergoing fire safety works, such as renovation works involving a fire-rated door, are required under the Fire Code to install Home Fire Alarm Devices (HFADs) within the units.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For residential units built before June 2018 and which have not undergone fire safety works since June 2018, the installation of HFADs is voluntary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We do not have data on the percentage of HDB flats built before June 2018 which have HFADs installed.

sections.label: HDB corridor fires and outreach
sections.summary: In 2021 there were 122 HDB common corridor and passageway fires, with electrical origins, naked light and lighted materials as top causes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2021, there were 122 fires that occurred at HDB common corridors and passageways.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If you look at the breakdown of the top three causes of fires: (a) we had 43 fires due to electrical origins, for example, fires involving PMD and electrical risers; (b) we had 42 fires due to naked light, for example, candle flame, flame from lighters; (c) we had 32 fires due to indiscriminate disposal of lighted materials, for example, cigarette butts; and (d) we had five fires due to other causes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The number of fires at HDB common corridors and passageways has been decreasing over the years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: With regard to how we work with the agencies, we have been working with HDB, Town Councils, MCSTs and many other stakeholders to educate and raise the awareness of how we can play our part in minimising or responding to fires.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: When the COVID-19 situation stablises, we will launch the Community Resilience Day.
